_comment: Backfill ledger for GH #422, acceptance criterion 3: 'The existing 8 unmarked replies on the
task-228 doc are handled explicitly (either back-filled with markers or recorded as
unattributable) rather than silently classified.'
WHY THEY ARE RECORDED HERE INSTEAD OF BACK-FILLED WITH MARKERS
The Google Docs/Drive comment surface exposed to this agent has create and reply calls but no
comment-UPDATE call, so a provenance marker cannot be added to a comment after the fact. The
marker is only available to comments posted from now on. These eight predate it, so the only
honest handling is to record them by exact id -- which is what a ledger is for, and it is the
signal that survives a body edit anyway.
EVIDENCE THAT THESE EIGHT ARE AGENT-AUTHORED (not inferred from writing style)
Two independent records agree, and they agree on the SPLIT as well as the total:
1. journal/task-228.md records two answering passes -- 'your three comments, answered in the
doc' and 'your five new comments, all answered' -- i.e. 3 + 5 = 8 agent replies.
2. The live comment dump clusters the eight reply timestamps into exactly two tight batches
matching those passes: 08:16:56-08:17:11Z (3 replies) and 17:14:29-17:15:11Z (5 replies).
Shiv's own eight comments are spread across 06:56-16:18Z, as human typing is.
The batch timing is corroboration, NOT the test -- it is recorded because it independently
reproduces the 3+5 split the journal states. Nothing here classifies by prose style; #463
measured that approach misfiring on 17 of 18 samples, which is why it is not used.
The eight top-level comments are deliberately NOT listed. Absence from this ledger does not
assert they are human -- the reader treats an unlisted, unmarked comment as 'unknown', never as
'human'. See the header of lib-doc-comments.mjs.
